bf109.role: German fighter, the G-14 version of 1944

combat.title: Air combat
combat.hint: You are at the controls facing a {{enemy}}: get behind it and keep it in the gunsight: every moment spent in the gunsight counts, and when the count is full your aircraft fires by itself and it is shot down, before time runs out.
combat.controls: Steer with the arrow keys or with the stick under the view. The pilot's head, in the middle of the instrument panel, turns toward the enemy.
combat.toast: Enemy fighters in sight: {{pilot}} can take the controls.

duel.toast: Enemy bomber in sight: {{pilot}} can attack.
duel.title: Bomber interception
duel.hint: You attack a {{enemy}} from behind. Play your {{moves}} moves: after the last one, the bomber is shot down if it is in your red firing cone, else it gets away.

maneuverHints.turnLeft: 1 cell ahead, then a quarter turn left
maneuverHints.turnRight: 1 cell ahead, then a quarter turn right

attack.raidText: Fighters attack the camp: its defense goes down, a building is destroyed and sometimes an aircraft on the ground. The more aircraft you send, the more the defense goes down.
attack.raidSend_one: Send {{count}} aircraft on a raid ({{time}} there and back)
attack.raidSend_other: Send {{count}} aircraft on a raid ({{time}} there and back)
attack.captureText: Your aircraft attack the camp: each aircraft standing on it is an air combat to win, and a combat lost loses the aircraft. When no defender is left the camp is yours and your remaining aircraft land on it.
attack.captureSend_one: Send {{count}} aircraft to take the camp ({{time}})
attack.captureSend_other: Send {{count}} aircraft to take the camp ({{time}})
attack.nobodyFree: No aircraft or no pilot is free.

wind.pushes: Wind of {{speed}} km/h: it pushes you to the {{side}}

strafe.title: Ground attack
strafe.hint: You strafe a {{nationality}} convoy that drives toward you: get on its lane, and your aircraft fires by itself at what is ahead. Destroy {{required}} of {{total}} before it has gone by. Spare the Red Cross ambulance: destroying it fails the attack.
strafe.controls: Steer with the left and right arrow keys, or with the stick under the view.
strafe.toast: A {{nationality}} convoy on the road: {{pilot}} can strafe it.

flak.title: Flak
flak.hint: The enemy guns fire at your aircraft: a red ring on the sky marks where each shell will burst, get out of it. The guns aim where you will be: they fire at random at first, then more and more accurately if you keep your line, so change it. Two hits destroy your aircraft ({{destroyed}}), the first damages it.
flak.controls: Steer with the left and right arrow keys, or with the stick under the view.
flak.toast: Flak is firing at the aircraft of {{pilot}}: it can dodge it.

photo.title: Photo reconnaissance
photo.hint: You fly over enemy ground: the camera of your aircraft takes by itself the target it keeps in its frame for a moment. Take {{required}} photos of {{total}} without being spotted: each tower you fly over raises the detection by {{percent}} %, and at 100 % you are spotted.
photo.controls: Steer with the left and right arrow keys, or with the stick under the view: the photo is taken by itself.
photo.toast: Enemy ground under the aircraft: {{pilot}} can photograph it.
photo.escaped: Reconnaissance failed: you were spotted, or photos are missing.

errors.invalidNickname: The nickname is 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, hyphen and underscore.
errors.invalidPassword: The password is required, 72 characters at most.
errors.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts: try again in a quarter of an hour.
errors.invalidBody: Fill in the nickname and the password.

squadron.signInHint: Sign in to see your squadron.

roster.title: Kill board
roster.hint: The pilots from the highest rank down, with their missions and their victories. Click one to open the pilot's sheet.

ace.title: {{name}} is an ace!
ace.text: Five victories over enemy fighters: {{name}} enters the legend of the squadron. Accuracy and resilience improve.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.text: {{name}} is promoted to {{rank}}. Accuracy and resilience improve.

crash.title: {{aircraft}} lost
crash.textKilled: The {{aircraft}} of {{name}} crashed far from the camp. {{name}} could not bail out in time.
crash.textBailed: The {{aircraft}} of {{name}} crashed far from the camp. {{name}} bailed out in time and is making their way back to the camp.

death.title: {{name}} has fallen
death.text: {{name}} will not come back. The name is written in the memorial of the squadron.

welcome.title: Welcome, commander
welcome.text: Germany is attacking in the west. You command this air base and its squadron of D.520s. The battle never ends: each enemy aircraft you shoot down counts in your score. You keep the squadron's journal: each return from a mission writes a page in it. I will guide you through the first day.

launch.title: Step 1: a first mission
launch.text: Open the control tower (the gold arrow) and prepare a reconnaissance, the least risky: pick a pilot and an aircraft, then launch the mission.

fly.title: Step 2: the squadron is in flight
fly.text: The flight lasts a few minutes, in real time. At the control tower, watch the fatigue and stress of the pilots: a tired pilot flies worse.

receive.title: Step 3: the return
receive.text: The squadron is back: open the control tower and authorize it to land, to read the report and collect the rewards.

maintenance.title: Step 4: the aircraft is damaged
maintenance.text: At the Hangar, inspect the aircraft to see its damage. If a module is destroyed, have the part made at the Workshop, then repair. An aircraft on fire explodes if it is not repaired in time.

free.title: Step 5: over to you
free.text: You have been through it all: missions, inspection, repair. To win you need 8 enemy aircraft shot down, which air combats bring. Rest your pilots, recruit, and improve the base with command points.

guide.here: The guide points at this building

reset.title: Start from scratch?
reset.text: This base is wiped: the squadron, the resources, the upgrades, the missions and the enemy aircraft shot down all start again from zero, and the tutorial is offered to you again. This cannot be undone.

journal.title: Diary
journal.hint: The pages the pilots write when they come back from each mission, and the notes of the camp.
journal.empty: The pages are still blank: the first mission to come back will fill them.

opening: Orders came to go on reconnaissance {{dayPart}}, in the {{aircraft}}. Look hard, stay unseen.
Reconnaissance {{dayPart}}. The {{aircraft}} purred nicely on takeoff, which is always a comfort.
I took off {{dayPart}} to see what the enemy is preparing. No shooting expected, in theory.
Off on reconnaissance {{dayPart}}. Fly low, keep your eyes open, come home. That is the whole plan.
success: I found what we were looking for, and it looks useful: command looked pleased when it read my report.
Everything I wanted to see, I saw. I marked it on my map while it was still fresh.
The ground gave up its secrets: columns, depots, smoke. It will make a good page for headquarters.
failure: I saw very little: haze and the fear of lifting my head do not mix. I am ashamed to come back empty-handed.
Back at base with nothing precise. My map is almost blank, and I know it will cost us.
Nothing worth reporting. I wonder whether I looked badly or the enemy hid well.

opening: Alert {{dayPart}}: bombers on their way. We got off the ground in a rush in the {{aircraft}}, without time to finish the coffee.
Orders to intercept bombers {{dayPart}}. The {{aircraft}} climbed as hard as it could.
Interception {{dayPart}}. Engine flat out, eyes on the horizon, searching for black dots.
success: We got them before they reached their target. Their formation came apart, and I saw the first plumes of smoke.
The bombers turned back, some of them burning. For once nobody had their bombs on their head.
I took them from behind, the way we were taught, and held my burst until I was close. They could not hold.
failure: The bombers got through. I could not stop them, and I know what they will leave behind.
Too late, too far, too few aircraft. They did their job, and we failed at ours.
They slipped through my fingers. I keep chewing over the burst I missed.

opening: Combat {{dayPart}} against enemy fighters. The {{aircraft}} was ready; I was a little less so.
We ran into fighters {{dayPart}}. A duel, no less, in the {{aircraft}}.
Fighter patrol {{dayPart}}, and the enemy made no pretence of avoiding us.
success: I caught the enemy in my sights at the right moment and the burst did the rest. I watched it fall.
A tight turn, a moment to aim, and it was over: the enemy aircraft went down in flames, and I could no longer feel my hands.
In the end the sky stayed mine and the other one left the game. I take no joy in it, but I can breathe.
failure: The enemy aircraft got away from me. I followed too far and fired too soon; I wasted my chance.
My opponent was better than me today, that is all. I could not get them into my sights.
No result. My opponent defended well, and my rounds went into empty air.

opening: Ground attack {{dayPart}}, skimming the treetops in the {{aircraft}}. You can see faces down there, and it is never pleasant.
A mission over the enemy lines {{dayPart}}. The {{aircraft}} brushed the fields, trees streaming under the wings.
They gave me a ground attack {{dayPart}}. Trucks, convoys, everything that rolls and shoots.
success: The trucks caught fire one after another. I pulled up with my heart in my throat.
Target hit, and well hit. The column is cut, which will slow their advance a little.
Pass after pass, I did my work. It is not glorious, but it is useful.
failure: My rounds fell wide, into the fields. My pass only raised dust, and the column went on its way.
Too high, too fast: target missed. The flak made it quite clear that I was in the way.
I hit nothing that matters. We will have to go back and do better.

opening: Raid on an enemy camp {{dayPart}}, the {{aircraft}} skimming the rooftops. The hangars slid by under the wings.
Raid mission {{dayPart}}. The {{aircraft}} crossed the lines, with the flak grumbling somewhere below.
Off on a raid {{dayPart}}. It is time to pay them back in kind.
success: The passes told: smoke is rising from the camp, and their flak fell silent for a moment.
Target hit, buildings on fire. They will think twice before trying again.
I made my passes without shaking, and the camp has the marks to show for it.
failure: My bursts fell wide. The camp hardly felt a thing.
Too much flak, too little time: I had to break away without destroying anything serious.
Raid missed. We will have to come back, in greater numbers.

opening: Camp capture {{dayPart}}. The {{aircraft}} flies alone toward the field: there is no leaving a camp once it is taken.
Special mission {{dayPart}}: put the {{aircraft}} down on a field that is no longer defended.
Off {{dayPart}} to take a camp. At the end of the flight there is a runway, and that is all I need.
success: The wheels touched the runway and nobody fired. The camp is ours.
Down, engine off, pennant planted: the field has changed hands.
We won a camp this morning, with its stores. Now we have to hold it.
failure: I could not land: the camp still holds. Back to base, empty-handed.
Too much fire over the field. I had to turn back.
Camp capture failed. The field stays theirs.

calm: Not a breath of wind; the air was smooth as oil.
The sky was calm, almost indecent given what we were about to do in it.
strong: The wind kept tossing the aircraft about. I had to hold the stick with both hands.
With a wind like that the aircraft kept drifting. I did not like it.

alone: Nobody on my wing, only the sound of the engine for company.
No wingman this time: you have to watch your own back.
together: There were several of us, with {{comrades}} alongside. It helps to know someone is on your wing.
Also up there: {{comrades}}. We talk little in flight, but we watch each other a lot.

long: {{minutes}} minutes in the air: the fuel gauge winked at me the whole way home.
A long sortie, {{minutes}} minutes at least. I felt it in my shoulders on the way back.

high: I had been warned this was a dangerous mission, and nobody had lied to me.
A high-risk mission: I knew it before I even climbed in, from the look on the chief's face.

none: Not a scratch on the {{aircraft}}, worth noting.
The aircraft came back without a mark. The mechanics will be bored.
light: A few splinters hit the {{aircraft}}, nothing serious.
My aircraft took a few hits: some holes, enough to keep the mechanics busy.
heavy: The {{aircraft}} is in a sorry state: a wing pierced, the engine coughing. I do not know how it brought me home.
I brought back a shredded aircraft. The mechanics looked at the {{aircraft}}, then looked up at me.
burning: The {{aircraft}} was smoking on final, a smell of burning oil in the cockpit. It has to be put out before it blows up on the runway.
Flames licked the cowling on landing. The crews ran, and so did I.
lost: I had to jump. The {{aircraft}} went down in flames in a field, and I landed under the silk, legs like jelly.
The aircraft is lost, that much is certain. I opened the canopy, jumped, and felt nothing until I was on the ground.

one: We lost {{lost}}. I cannot write it without the pen shaking.
{{lost}} will not be coming back. A place at the mess will stay empty.
Someone will have to write to the family of {{lost}}. It is not for me to do, but I am already thinking of it.
several: We lost {{lost}}. I cannot write it without the pen shaking.
{{lost}} will not be coming back. Their places at the mess will stay empty.
Someone will have to write to the families of {{lost}}. It is not for me to do, but I am already thinking of it.

stressed: My nerves are in knots; my hand shakes on the paper.
My nerves are raw: every engine noise makes me jump.
tired: Tiredness weighs me down: I write these lines with my eyes closing.
I have no strength left, just enough to hold the pen before I sleep.
fine: I feel well, surprisingly, as if the sky had given me my strength back.
Nothing to report on that side: the body holds, and so does the head.

success: Tomorrow we do it again. Someone has to.
I close this book with a little pride, and I almost resent having any.
A good day, the kind we get too rarely.
failure: Tomorrow we will have to do better. I see no other way out.
I close this book with a taste of ash.
It was not the day for it. There will be others, I want to believe.

blank: This page stayed blank. None of the pilots came back to write it. Missing from the roll call: {{lost}}.
Not a line that day. Nobody could open this book. Missing from the roll call: {{lost}}.
The pencil stayed in its place. Nobody came back from this mission to pick it up. Missing from the roll call: {{lost}}.

choose.title: Choose your base
choose.hint: Each free site is a base to run; the other players of this world have taken theirs.

world.legend: Your camps are ringed in gold, your allies' (players or the AI) in green and the enemy's in red; a free camp has no glow; a camp that is held carries the badge of its side, the roundel of the Allies or the cross of the Axe; a camp that a raid has just hit is in ruins. Click a camp: its details open on the other side of the map.
world.pick: Click a free camp on the map to put your base there.
world.landToClaim: To take a free camp, send an aircraft there from the Hangar: it is yours while one of your aircraft stands on it, and you can hold {{max}} at most.

lifeTopics.0: {{pilot}} spent the evening mending the radio of the mess: it still crackles, but it works.
lifeTopics.1: A farmer from the neighbourhood brought eggs to the squadron; the cook made an omelette for everyone.
lifeTopics.2: The rain soaked the tents last night; the mechanics dried everything in the morning sun.
lifeTopics.3: {{pilot}} wrote to the family; the letter will go with the next mail truck.
lifeTopics.4: A supply convoy stopped at the camp; the driver brought news from the front.
lifeTopics.5: The dog of the base stole a sausage from the mess again; nobody wanted to punish it.
lifeTopics.6: {{pilot}} won the chocolate ration of the whole table at cards.
lifeTopics.7: The wind knocked down the windsock; the mechanics put it back up before the first patrol.
lifeTopics.8: An improvised game of football pitted the mechanics against the pilots; the mechanics won.
lifeTopics.9: A storm broke over the camp; the squadron watched it from the hangar, coffee in hand.
lifeTopics.10: {{pilot}} found a harmonica in a sack from the store and plays it in the evening in front of the tents.
lifeTopics.11: The officer of the guard walked round the aircraft at dawn; he said nothing, but shook the hand of every mechanic.

stationing.title: Station an aircraft
stationing.text: An aircraft and its pilot land at another camp, with fuel and ammunition for it, and stay there until you recall them. On a free camp, they take it for you while they are there. While they are away they do not fly, rest or get given; once landed, the camp they are at flies them on its missions, with its pilots.

supply.title: Supply the camp
supply.text: An aircraft and its pilot bring resources to this camp, then turn round at once: the round trip lasts twice the flight. The aircraft takes {{max}} of each at most, and what does not fit in the warehouse where it lands is lost.
